comments.author: Keith Adams
comments.html:
"The most interesting discussion resulted from Keith's presentation of vprobes -- a DTrace... um... inspired facility in VMware."
Glad you enjoyed the talk! And to be clear, there's no elliptical "um" about it: DTrace did, indeed, inspire VProbes, and without DTrace's precedent, VProbes would probably be very different. I hope I didn't come off otherwise.
On a more important note: I forgot my t-shirt at the conference :(. Whose car might I wash to get one? Men's small or medium would do ...

comments.author: ahl
comments.html: @Keith I was trying to suggest another descriptor, but stopped short. As to your t-shirt, I've got your back, but it might be a bit roomy -- only larges were left. Let me know where you want it sent.

comments.author: John Birrell
comments.html:
I am currently in Sunnyvale, CA doing endless rounds of interviews.
Next week I'll be in Ottawa for the http://bsdcan.org/ conference where I'll be presenting a paper on the DTrace port to FreeBSD. The conference includes other flavours of BSD, so hopefully the others will show some interest.
I've arranged to meet with Colin Burgess to discuss the porting project and how we might proceed with that.

comments.author: John Birrell
comments.html:
I forgot to mention that there is also a Google Summer of Code project approved to port the DTrace Toolkit to FreeBSD.
The clean-room implementation of CTF parsing missed the cut-off though, unfortunately.
